question: Describe how you would build our new public website on AEM Sites with Edge Delivery Services, including the blocks and page templates our marketing team will author with.
kb:
Our approach
- We would build the site on Edge Delivery Services with its code managed and deployed directly from a GitHub repository. New content is added instantly, without a rebuild process.
- Your authors add and edit every block in your library in the Universal Editor, and pages publish to Edge Delivery as designed.

How we would do it
- Inventory the blocks in your library, and agree with your authors which fields each block should let them edit.
- Give each block its Universal Editor definition, model and filter, so authors can add and edit it in AEM with the agreed fields.
- Keep the block code and styles in the Edge Delivery build, and test adding and editing each block in the Universal Editor on a sample page.
- Publish the sample pages and check that every block renders on Edge Delivery as expected, then hand your authors a short block guide.
- Map each part of the design to Core Components, editable templates or a custom component, and agree the map with your design team.
- Agree the site structure and paths with your team, and whether stage and production are split into separate sites.

What you get
- Universal Editor definitions, models and filters for each block
- Block inventory with agreed author fields
- Published sample pages and test results
- Author block guide
- The built site on Core Components and editable templates

Timeline and effort
- This runs during the build.
- Planning estimate: 480 hours.

Risk we manage
- A block that edits well but breaks on the published page: we publish a sample page for every block before your authors build real pages.

question: Our current site runs on Drupal 9 and holds about 3,400 pages and 900 PDF documents, including state rate filings. Describe how you would migrate this content, what you would retire, and how you would preserve URLs.
kb:
Our approach
- We would start with discovery: a review of your current site's content, templates and integrations, a named team with agreed roles, and the measures of success.
- Your agreed pages are on the new site with their titles, descriptions and structured data in place, and every retired URL redirects to its new page.

How we would do it
- Map your current site to the new one page by page, using your analytics and search data, and mark each page to keep, merge or retire.
- Run Adobe's importer on an example of each page type so your authors can agree the structure, then migrate the agreed pages into Edge Delivery documents and blocks.
- Carry over or rewrite titles, descriptions, headings and structured data for each migrated page, with your reviewers approving the rewritten copy.
- Build the redirect map, with every retired URL in the redirects spreadsheet, and set up bulk metadata and sitemaps for the new site.
- Run crawl, link and Lighthouse checks before launch, fix what falls short of the agreed thresholds, and test that every redirect resolves.
- Agree the site structure and paths with your team, and whether stage and production are split into separate sites.

What you get
- Migrated pages in Edge Delivery documents and blocks
- Redirect map
- Metadata and sitemap records
- Pre-launch check report
- AEM site created from the Edge Delivery template

Timeline and effort
- This runs during the build.
- Planning estimate: 320 hours.

Risk we manage
- Losing search value when URLs change: every retired URL gets a redirect, and crawl and link checks must pass before launch.

question: Describe your go-live and cutover plan, including redirects, search engine protection and rollback.
kb:
Our approach
- Your site goes live through a tested production pipeline, with CDN, SSL and DNS in place, redirects for retired URLs and rollback criteria ready.

How we would do it
- Work through Adobe's go-live checklist with your team, giving each item an owner in a cutover plan.
- Run the production pipeline with functional and UI tests, complete Dispatcher validation, and set up notification profiles and traffic filter rules.
- Run performance and security tests on stage, which has the same sizing as production, and user acceptance testing on a test subdomain.
- Agree rollback criteria and redirects for retired URLs beforehand, then set up CDN and SSL and complete the DNS cutover.
- Agree the site structure and paths with your team, and whether stage and production are split into separate sites.
- Inventory the blocks in your library, and agree with your authors which fields each block should let them edit.

What you get
- Completed go-live checklist with owners
- Cutover plan with rollback criteria
- Performance, security and acceptance test results
- Redirects for retired URLs
- AEM site created from the Edge Delivery template

Timeline and effort
- This runs as the build closes, through launch.
- Planning estimate: 160 hours.

Risk we manage
- A cutover problem with no way back: we agree rollback criteria beforehand and test on stage and a test subdomain before the DNS cutover.

What we would need from you
- Access to your DNS settings and SSL certificates, and the people who manage them
- Testers for user acceptance testing, and the person who approves go-live
- Access to AEM Author and to your Edge Delivery code

question: Describe how you would use Adobe Brand Visibility to measure how AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity describe Cedar Prairie and our products, and how you would report it to us.
kb:
Our approach
- Adobe's Brand Presence page lists ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini and Perplexity as supported.
- Your CJA reports show AI-agent activity beside AI-referred visits and conversions, as separate measures reconciled to Brand Visibility and your web data.

How we would do it
- Configure the Brand Visibility connection with your CJA administrator, adding the Adobe Brand Visibility source dataset to a CJA connection and data view.
- Map the AI-agent activity's URLs and hosts to your site, and check the bot measures reconcile to Brand Visibility.
- Build a derived field on AI referring domains that identifies AI-referred visits in your existing CJA web data, reconciled to your agreed web reports.
- Agree the metric definitions with your application owners, and deliver a first report that keeps AI-agent activity and AI-referred visits and conversions as separate measures.

What you get
- Validated Brand Visibility connection in CJA
- Derived field for AI-referred visits
- Agreed metric definitions
- Initial report with separate AI-agent and visit measures
- Notes on what each measure covers

Timeline and effort
- This runs during the build.
- Planning estimate: 56 hours.
- This needs CJA Select or higher.

Risk we manage
- Bot activity and human visits read as one number: we keep AI-agent activity and AI-referred visits and conversions as separate measures, each reconciled to its own source.
catalog:
Our approach
- Brand Visibility sends aggregate AI-agent activity (from CDN logs, by URL and host) into CJA through an Experience Platform source. AI-referred visits and conversions come from CJA's own web data, and Brand Visibility reads those results for its business impact view.
- Brand Visibility runs the prompts you choose on a recurring basis across the AI platforms it supports and records how your brand appears in each answer and how that changes over time. It measures the prompts you monitor: the questions people put to AI assistants themselves are not disclosed by the platforms.
- Adobe's Brand Presence page lists ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini and Perplexity as supported.
- The dashboards report the percentage of prompts where your brand is mentioned, how often your website is used as a source, share of voice and sentiment, and compare you with the other brands you choose to track in each market.

What we would do
- For Cedar Prairie Mutual Insurance Company, we will configure the supported Brand Visibility bot-data connection and map URLs and hosts; we will identify AI-referred visits in the existing CJA web data with a derived field on AI referring domains; and we will align observed AI-referral and conversion measures with existing CJA data.

What we would need from you
- Your Customer Journey Analytics package: CJA Select or higher.

What we would need from you
- Source facts and reviewers who approve accuracy and relevance
- Publishing access and your existing page templates

question: When a visitor asks for a person, the conversation should pass to a licensed agent in our Genesys Cloud contact center. Describe how you would design this handoff.

How we would do it
- Agree the route for Concierge data with your analytics team, either the bundled Concierge dataset or callback events, and document the dataset permissions.
- Bring the Concierge data into your Customer Journey Analytics through the agreed route, joined with your web or commerce data where permitted.
- Build Workspace reports for the agreed conversation, recommendation and purchase measures, limited to what the selected data supports.
- Add handoff rates where the handoff outcome has a documented source, a permitted ingestion and join route and a metric definition.

What you get
- Documented data route and dataset permissions
- Workspace reports on conversation, recommendation and purchase measures
- Measure definitions

Timeline and effort
- This runs during the build.
- Planning estimate: 40 hours.
- This needs CJA Select or higher (more than one event dataset in a connection).

Risk we manage
- Joining Concierge data where its license does not permit it: we agree the route and document the dataset permissions before any report is built.

What we would need from you
- Your analytics team's decision on the data route, and the dataset permissions that apply
- Your definitions of a purchase and, where measured, a successful handoff
catalog:
Our approach
- Brand Concierge's built-in analytics dashboard is powered by Customer Journey Analytics and needs no separate CJA license. Analysis alongside your other journey data uses your separately licensed CJA. Concierge events reach your CJA in one of two ways: through the bundled Concierge dataset, where its license permits joining it with your web or commerce data, or otherwise as callback events collected separately through your licensed collection route. We agree the route with you and document the dataset permissions before this work starts.

Licensing this needs
- Your Customer Journey Analytics package: CJA Select or higher (more than one event dataset in a connection).
